result: Transplantation of eight three kb segments from a 47 kb H3K27me2/3 domain on LG VIL to his-3 or csr-1 loci did not induce de novo H3K27me2/3, demonstrating that not all facultative heterochromatin is controlled by underlying sequence elements.
evaluation: Claims C8 and C9 are directly supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B and C. Claim C81 is a reasonable inference from these transplantation experiments. The experimental design is appropriate and the negative results are clearly demonstrated.

result: In the UK3-41 insertional translocation strain, the region of LG VIL displaced from the chromosome end lost H3K27me2/3, suggesting that normal methylation of this subtelomeric domain is position-dependent.
evaluation: Claims C10-C12 are supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 1A. The loss of H3K27me2/3 when the region is moved away from the chromosome end provides strong evidence for position-dependence. The inference in C12 is logical given the combined transplantation and translocation data.

result: In the OY350 quasiterminal translocation, the translocated LG VIL domain preserved its normal H3K27me2/3 distribution when placed adjacent to a different chromosome end, demonstrating that H3K27me2/3 depends on proximity to a chromosome end in a non-specific manner.
evaluation: Claims C13-C16 are supported by ChIP-seq data for OY350. The preservation of H3K27me2/3 at a different telomere provides strong evidence that proximity to any chromosome end is sufficient. The experimental design directly tests the hypothesis and the conclusion is well-supported.

result: Seven genome rearrangements independently showed de novo H3K27me2/3 at their new chromosome ends, extending an average of approximately 180 kb into new subtelomeric regions, while H3K27me2/3 distribution on unrelated chromosomes was unaltered, strongly suggesting that chromosome ends promote H3K27me deposition.
evaluation: Claims C17-C20 are supported by ChIP-seq data from multiple translocation strains shown in Figures 1B-E and Figure 1—figure supplements 2A-C and 3. The consistency across seven independent rearrangements provides strong evidence. The average distance calculation (C18) appears to be based on the data, though the methodology is not explicitly described.

result: Analysis of multiple translocations (ALS159, OY329, NM149, OY320) revealed that some H3K27me2/3 domains can be maintained when translocated to internal chromosomal sites (position-independent), while subtelomeric H3K27me2/3 closest to chromosome ends is consistently lost when moved away from telomeres (position-dependent).
evaluation: Claims C21-C29 are supported by ChIP-seq data from multiple translocation strains shown in Figures 1C-F. The consistent pattern of losing the most distal H3K27me2/3 while retaining internal domains across multiple independent translocations provides strong evidence for two classes of H3K27me2/3 domains. The distinction between position-dependent and position-independent domains is well-supported.

result: In a segmental duplication strain derived from OY329 crossed with Mauriceville, SNP-parsed ChIP-seq showed that duplicated chromosomal segments have distinct H3K27me2/3 profiles, demonstrating that the loss of H3K27me2/3 in OY329 is a bona fide position effect rather than a result of trans-acting factors.
evaluation: Claims C30-C34 are supported by SNP-parsed ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2B. This cis-trans test is a rigorous experimental design that effectively rules out trans-acting factors. The independent behavior of homologous segments in the same nucleus provides strong evidence for position effects.

result: Analysis of seven translocation strains by RNA-seq showed that gains of H3K27me2/3 at novel subtelomeres coincided with reduced transcript levels, while losses of H3K27me2/3 at previously subtelomeric regions were associated with increased transcript abundance, demonstrating that chromosomal rearrangements cause marked changes in both H3K27me2/3 and gene expression.
evaluation: Claims C35-C39 are supported by RNA-seq data from seven translocation strains shown in Figure 3. The comprehensive analysis across multiple strains and the consistent correlation between H3K27me2/3 changes and gene expression changes provide strong evidence. The qPCR validation (Figure 3—figure supplement 1) further supports the findings.

result: Deletion of tert resulted in loss of telomere repeats, chromosome circularization, and loss of subtelomeric H3K27me2/3 domains on all chromosomes except LG V, while internal H3K27me2/3 domains were unaffected, demonstrating that telomere repeats or linear chromosome ends are required for position-dependent H3K27me2/3.
evaluation: Claims C40-C43, C45-C47, and C71 are supported by Southern blot (Figure 4A), PCR (Figure 4B), and ChIP-seq data (Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1). The experimental design is rigorous, with appropriate controls including input DNA sequencing to rule out chromosome degradation. The exception of LG V (C44) is explained by its unique rDNA structure. This is a key experiment demonstrating the necessity of telomere repeats.

result: Ectopic insertion of telomere repeats at the csr-1 and his-3 loci induced local H3K27me2/3, with (TTAGGG)17 inducing a large domain (~225 kb) spanning 30 genes, demonstrating that telomere repeats are sufficient to trigger ectopic H3K27 methylation at internal chromosomal sites.
evaluation: Claims C48-C53, C72, C74, and C118 are supported by ChIP-qPCR data (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1) and ChIP-seq data (Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 2). The dose-response relationship (more repeats induce more H3K27me2/3) strengthens the conclusion. This is a critical experiment demonstrating sufficiency of telomere repeats. The size of the induced domain is comparable to natural subtelomeric domains lost in tert.

result: The combined evidence from translocation, tert deletion, and ectopic telomere repeat experiments demonstrates that telomere repeats underpin position-dependent H3K27me2/3, being both necessary and sufficient for subtelomeric H3K27me2/3, and that proximity to chromosome ends is necessary to maintain and sufficient to induce H3K27me2/3, providing an example of a cis-acting sequence that directs H3K27 methylation.
evaluation: Claims C70, C73, C82, C83, C115-C117, and C119 represent the major conclusions synthesized from multiple lines of evidence. The necessity is demonstrated by tert deletion experiments, sufficiency by ectopic telomere repeat insertion, and the distinction between position-dependent and position-independent domains by translocation experiments. The logic is sound and the conclusions are well-supported by converging evidence from multiple experimental approaches.

result: H3K27me2/3 covers approximately 7% of the N. crassa genome in greater than 200 domains ranging from 0.5 to 107 kb, including about 1000 fully-covered transcriptionally quiescent genes, with enrichment at subtelomeric regions as also reported for other fungi.
evaluation: Claims C1-C7 are supported by citations to previous studies (Jamieson et al., 2013; Galazka et al., 2016; Schotanus et al., 2015; Dumesic et al., 2015; Studt et al., 2016; Connolly et al., 2013). These are background claims establishing the context for the current study. The citations appear appropriate and the claims are consistent with established knowledge in the field.

result: PcG proteins, initially discovered in D. melanogaster as repressors of HOX genes, form PRC1 and PRC2 complexes that modify histones, with PRC2 being widely conserved in eukaryotes including N. crassa but absent in S. cerevisiae and S. pombe, and while PREs recruit PcG proteins in D. melanogaster and similar elements exist in A. thaliana, the mechanism in vertebrates remains elusive.
evaluation: Claims C55-C65 provide background on PcG proteins and are supported by appropriate citations to previous studies. These are well-established facts in the field and the citations appear accurate. This background contextualizes the significance of the current findings.

result: The control of H3K27 methylation is fundamentally different from that of epigenetic marks in constitutive heterochromatin, with H3K27 methylation being much more plastic than H3K9 methylation and often position-dependent, unlike DNA methylation and H3K9 methylation which are faithfully methylated de novo at ectopic sites.
evaluation: Claims C66-C69 are supported by both citations to previous studies and the experimental data presented in this manuscript. The comparison to constitutive heterochromatin marks is well-supported and provides important context for understanding the novelty of the findings. The position-dependence of H3K27me is demonstrated by the transplantation and translocation experiments.

result: Native N. crassa telomeres have an average of 20 repeats, and while H3K27me is non-essential in N. crassa despite silencing scores of genes, PREs in D. melanogaster are neither sufficient in all contexts nor fully penetrant, with deletion of a well-studied PRE not significantly affecting silencing or H3K27 methylation, and only a few candidate PRE-like elements identified in mammals.
evaluation: Claims C75-C80 are supported by appropriate citations to previous studies. These provide important context for the current work, establishing that N. crassa is a suitable model organism (H3K27me is non-essential) and that the control of H3K27 methylation is poorly understood even in well-studied organisms like D. melanogaster and mammals.

result: Gene silencing near chromosome ends (TPE) has been observed in fungi, D. melanogaster, M. musculus, and human cells, but previous studies did not implicate H3K27me, and the extent of heterochromatin spreading from telomeres in N. crassa is substantially greater than previously reported, possibly due to the absence of canonical subtelomere sequences, making these findings potentially the first documented case of H3K27me-mediated TPE.
evaluation: Claims C85-C94 are supported by appropriate citations and comparison with previous literature. The claim that this may be the first documented case of H3K27me-mediated TPE (C94) is appropriately qualified as speculative. The comparison with previous TPE studies and the explanation for the greater extent of spreading in N. crassa are reasonable.

result: Enrichment of H3K27 methylation at telomeres has been observed in fungi, plants, and animals, suggesting that recruitment of PRC2 to telomere repeats may be widespread, with possible mechanisms including indirect recruitment by telobox-binding transcription factors or direct binding to G-quadruplex RNA from telomere repeat transcription, and TERRA directly interacting with EZH2 with H3K27me3 peaks correlated with TERRA-associated chromatin in mouse ES cells.
evaluation: Claims C95-C101 are supported by appropriate citations to previous studies. These provide important context suggesting that the findings in N. crassa may have broader implications across eukaryotes. The proposed mechanisms (C98-C99) are appropriately presented as speculative possibilities. The TERRA findings (C100-C101) provide a potential molecular mechanism.

result: Interstitial telomere sequences are scattered in many organisms' genomes, but in N. crassa they are rare (less than four tandem repeats) and not preferentially associated with H3K27me2/3 regions, while in S. cerevisiae and S. pombe (which lack PRC2 and H3K27me) internal telomere repeat-like elements can promote heterochromatin formation, and in N. tabacum heterochromatic internal telomere repeats lack H3K27 methylation present at genuine telomeres, with insertion of about 130 telomere repeats in Chinese ovary cells failing to significantly alter local transcription.
evaluation: Claims C102-C108 are supported by appropriate citations and analysis of the N. crassa genome. These comparisons across organisms provide important context for understanding the specificity of telomere repeat effects on H3K27me2/3. The observation that interstitial telomere sequences in N. crassa are not associated with H3K27me2/3 (C104) is consistent with the finding that proximity to chromosome ends is important.

result: Genome rearrangements are common in malignant cells and can drive tumorigenesis through gene fusions, enhancer hijacking, and oncogene amplification, and the findings suggest that such rearrangements may additionally impact gene expression through effects on facultative heterochromatin, with some reports of human diseases driven by position effects, demonstrating that changes in genome organization can have sweeping effects on epigenetic marks and gene expression, suggesting unappreciated roles in evolution and cancer etiology.
evaluation: Claims C109-C110 are supported by appropriate citations. However, claims C111 and C114 are speculative extrapolations to cancer and evolution that are not directly tested in this study. While the speculation is reasonable given the findings, it remains uncertain without direct evidence in cancer cells or evolutionary contexts. Claim C112 provides some support with citations to human disease cases, but the connection to H3K27me-mediated position effects is not established.

result: The identification of telomere repeats as potent signals for H3K27 methylation represents a major advance in understanding facultative heterochromatin formation in eukaryotes and provides new insight into the relationship between genome organization and control of heterochromatin formation.
evaluation: Claims C84 and C120 are interpretive statements about the significance of the findings. These are supported by the comprehensive experimental evidence presented in the manuscript. The identification of telomere repeats as cis-acting elements for H3K27 methylation is indeed a significant advance given the limited understanding of H3K27me control mechanisms.

result: Only about 10% of H3K27me2/3-marked genes are upregulated when the H3K27 methyltransferase is removed, supporting the notion that transcriptional shut-off may precede PRC2 recruitment, though low transcriptional activity cannot entirely explain PRC2 targeting since many low-expressed genes are not H3K27 methylated in N. crassa.
evaluation: Claims C121 and C123 are supported by citations to previous studies (Klocko et al., 2016; Jamieson et al., 2013) and analysis of gene expression and ChIP-seq data. Claim C122 is appropriately presented as speculative. These observations provide important context for understanding the relationship between H3K27me and transcription, though they do not directly address the mechanism of PRC2 recruitment.

result: LG V is unique in that one of its ends is capped with approximately 150 copies of the approximately 9 kb rDNA repeat, and the size of the H3K27me2/3 domain induced by (TTAGGG)17 is comparable to the size of subtelomeric H3K27me2/3 domains that were lost in the tert strain.
evaluation: Claim C44 is supported by citation to previous study (Butler and Metzenberg, 1990) and explains the exception of LG V in the tert experiments. Claim C54 is a comparison of ChIP-seq data from different experiments that strengthens the conclusion that ectopic telomere repeats can recapitulate natural subtelomeric H3K27me2/3 domains. Both claims are well-supported.
